new_statements.quote: 2. FONOLOGI DAN MORFOLOGI BAHASA MANDAILING. Oleh: Livain Lubis. Pembimbing: Drs. Husein Widjajakusumah. Tahun: 1963. ... Dialek yang digunakan di daerah ini dikenal sebagai dialek Angkola-Mandailing. Bahasa Mandailing memiliki fonem-fonem segmental yang berupa lima fonem vokal dan 18 fonem konsonan, di samping fonem supra segmental berupa tekanan, yang simultan timbul dengan gejala kwantita pada vokal.
new_statements.translation: 2. Phonology and morphology of the Mandailing language. By Livain Lubis. Supervisor Drs. Husein Widjajakusumah. Year 1963. ... The dialect used in this area is known as the Angkola-Mandailing dialect. Mandailing has segmental phonemes consisting of five vowel phonemes and 18 consonant phonemes, besides a suprasegmental phoneme in the form of stress, which arises simultaneously with the phenomenon of quantity (length) on the vowel.

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the catalog's 'lexical' coding from van der Tuuk 1864 (klemtoon on last or penultimate syllable depending on word class/function): the abstract classes stress as a suprasegmental PHONEME co-occurring with vowel length, i.e. distinctive rather than fixed, and adds the phonetic detail that stress goes with vowel quantity. Placement itself is not visible, so this is weak, abstract-level support only; pp. 13-43 of the typescript would be needed to confirm.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Per the thesis abstract, Lubis analyses Mandailing (Angkola-Mandailing dialect) as having 5 vowel and 18 consonant phonemes plus one suprasegmental phoneme, stress (tekanan), realised together with vowel quantity. Treating stress as a phoneme implies it is taken as distinctive; the visible text does not say on which syllable stress falls, so placement (final vs penult, word-class conditioning as in van der Tuuk 1864) cannot be confirmed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: not mentioned in the visible abstract text
new_statements.identity_note: Lubis 1963 describes the 'dialek Angkola-Mandailing' of the region south of Tapanuli (per its abstract); Coppell 1981 notes some contrastive material with Toba Batak. The catalog record itself rests on van der Tuuk's 1864 Mandailing notes appended to his Toba grammar ('De klemtoon is hier als in T.').

sources.quote: p.147-148: 'Tekanan pada kata yang bersuku dua dalam bahasa Batak Angkola dapat dibedakan atas dua jenis, yaitu (1) nomina dan verba mendapat tekanan yang lebih keras pada suku pertama ... /i-gung/ hidung, /ba-gas/ rumah, /ma-nuk/ ayam, /ma-ngan/ makan, /mo-dom/ tidur; (2) adjektiva dan kata tambahan mendapat tekanan yang lebih keras pada suku kedua: /je-ges/ cantik, /jor-but/ jelek, /ba-gas/ dalam, /si-gop/ cepat, /lam-bat/ lambat ... nomina dan verba mempunyai tekanan (1-3), sedangkan adjektiva dan kata tambahan mempunyai tekanan (3-1).' p.148-149: three-syllable words strongest stress on th

sources.note: Only modern phonology of the Angkola-Mandailing cluster with an explicit stress section (pp.147-149); our Mandailing coding rests on an 1864 one-line cross-reference to the Toba chapter. downloaded now; confirms word-class-conditioned penult/final contrast (bagas 'house' vs bagas 'inside') and penult in longer words.

sources.note: Describes Batak Angkola (ISO akb, Tapanuli Selatan), a distinct Glottolog languoid and the closest sister variety of Mandailing (btm); the book's own cataloguing heading is 'Bahasa Batak Angkola-Mandailing-Fonologi' and the 2016 regional dictionary treats Angkola-Mandailing as one lexicon. The catalog record for Mandailingsch has an empty rule and no existing statements, so there is nothing to agree with or contradict; this is the best available proxy statement and should be recorded as Angkola-based, not as a Mandailing-proper source. scanned artefacts in the ('umurnnya', 'ernpat', 'dalarn'…
